speaker: Doctor
text: I am ready to begin your assessment for your gait and limb ataxia. To start, can you describe exactly how your balance and coordination have changed over time, and do you have any specific medical conditions in your history?

speaker: Patient
text: I started having trouble walking recently, and people say I look drunk when I walk. I also feel clumsy in my arms and legs, especially on the right side.

speaker: Doctor
text:
You mentioned the clumsiness is especially on the right side; is this ataxia constant, or does it worsen significantly when you walk in the dark? Additionally, do you have a history of diabetes or any past strokes?

REQUEST TEST: HbA1c

speaker: Doctor
text: The HbA1c results are normal, so diabetes is unlikely. Does the "drunk" walking feel like you are staggering side-to-side (lateral), or more like you are falling forward or backward? Also, have you noticed any changes in your vision, such as double vision or trouble focusing?

speaker: Patient
text: I have Crohn disease and it has been difficult to control. I have been taking natalizumab for about a year.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: PML (Progressive Multifocal Leukoencephalopathy) secondary to natalizumab use.

The significant history of Crohn's disease treated with natalizumab, combined with new onset gait and limb ataxia, strongly suggests a demyelinating event. I need to visualize the brain to confirm this. REQUEST IMAGES: MRI_Brain_with_contrast.
